# 4 Maccabees Chapter 12 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Sinaiticus) | **Section:** The Brothers' Inner Resolve and Praise

---

**12:1** For truly the contest in which they were involved was divine, and the virtue by which they were tested was the virtue of endurance.

**12:2** The prizes for which they were contending were incorruptible prizes — prizes of immortality and of undying glory.

**12:3** But even if none of these things had been true, even if the law had said nothing about rewards and punishments, even then their reason would have been worthy to crown them with virtue.

**12:4** For they suffered for the sake of virtue, and they overcame the tyrant by the power of reason.

**12:5** The seven brothers are more admirable than the greatest heroes — for they overcame passion not with iron weapons but with the weapons of noble reason.

**12:6** They are more victorious than those who conquered at Thermopylae — for the Spartans fought with weapons of iron, but these fought with the weapons of reason and virtue.

**12:7** The noble Eleazar is first in the battle, the mother of the seven brothers is second in command, and the seven brothers form the sacred company.

**12:8** The tyrant was the enemy, the world was the arena, and devotion to God was the weapon.

**12:9** Their praise is in all the world, for they lived the life of virtue and died for the law.

**12:10** For by dying for justice they gained life and fame everlasting.

**12:11** They proved that reason is the true master of the passions, not only in theory but in their very deaths.

**12:12** They showed that piety is truly unbreakable when tested to the extreme.

**12:13** O mother, what words can praise you fittingly? You bore witness to the faithfulness of the law in your very body.

**12:14** You sealed by your own death the proof that reason masters passion.

**12:15** For you, like a wrestler in the stadium, endured every blow of the tyrant's passion and yet were not overthrown.

**12:16** You held firm; you did not waver; you proved the sovereignty of reason over passion in your very flesh.

**12:17** For as long as our nation endures, the memory of Eleazar and the seven brothers and their mother will be imperishable.

**12:18** Happy are those who received this honor! For they are now with God and with Abraham and Isaac and Jacob.

**12:19** The blessed ones proved by the nobility of their dying that reason can master the passions.

**12:20** And so I end my argument here: devotion to God, through the instruction of reason, is sovereign over all the passions.

**12:21** This demonstration is proved by the heroic deaths of Eleazar and the seven brothers and the mother who was worthy of them.

**12:22** Let no one despise the weakness of old age or the tenderness of youth in matters of virtue — for these heroes prove that neither age nor youth is an impediment to virtue.
